scope: Proposition 5.6 (Stationary data) of the manuscript “The Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions” (preprints/The-Kakeya-maximal-conjecture-in-three-dimensions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 074 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 49cc52aa3de89f0e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 47-48. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: There is a realizing sequence of canonical equalities and compatible packet assignments for which the preceding collapsed law, event labels, and matrix forms have the following properties. All local upper bounds and original index weights are retained. (i) Along an index, occupied time blocks have regular branching exponent s0 = 1 − β ≥ 0. More precisely, for fixed c < b ≤ 1, an occupied Ic contains Nℓ(1−β)(b−c)+o(1) (5.20) occupied Ib blocks. The event normals on that index in Ic lie in a range of size ΘcNo(1). (ii) For 0 < c ≤ 1 there are assigned packets Bc on the occupied Ic blocks, with raw active index mass at least nc = ∆hN(B∗+τ)c+dw(1−c) (5.21) in exponent. On each fixed time block the assigned index sets are disjoint, and each retained index has one packet owner there. The used normals of a packet differ from its spatial normal by at most ΘcNo(1). (iii) In every used event frame, the widths of Bc in the four forms (5.18) are bounded by LX(c), LY (c), LU (c), LV (c) up to subpower expansion. Equivalently, their negative log exponents are ρ + wc, ρ + (w − τ)c, ρ + (w − ℓ)c, ρ + (w − 1)c, (5.22) 47 (iv) The data and packet lower bounds coexist on any prescribed finite list of scales and tests, and hence on countable lists by slow diagonals. They persist, in exponent, on typical nondeficient parts after extensive regular refinements. All packet memberships are memberships of original active indices on their physical intervals. In a chart registered at Ic, the packet at a finer Ib is determined by the index, chart, and Ib; a matrix cell in that chart is determined by the index and chart.
